title: [CLO Beginner's Guide] Analog Control_Analog Stability
description:
CLO Beginner's Guide: By studying courses related to [Simulation Control], master more practical garment adjustment tools, comprehensively apply them to improve simulation stability and optimize garment shape. Gradually advance to mastering garment production techniques.  
Course reference:  
[CLO Tips Mini Class - The Ingenious Use of Layer Settings] https://www.bilibili.com/video/BV1ZEcne5EVg/?share_source=copy_web
transcript:
Hello everyone, this video will introduce you to 3D clothing production and related tools for simulation control.

First, in the Connect tab, under the CloudTraining account, unlock the keyword simulation control.  
Double-click to download and open the frozen and back-up file.  
In the 3D window, select the belt of this shirt skirt.  
Right-click to select Frozen, and press Ctrl-K.  
The frozen version will appear light blue on the surface.  
After opening the simulation, its position and shape will be completely fixed, and dragging will not change or shift it.  
However, it should be noted that there is still physical contact and collision between it and the normal soft clothing beneath.  

Then right-click on the plate again.  
Unlock the belt.  
Right-click to switch to the back-up plate.  
Right-click, press Ctrl-J.  
The back-up plate becomes translucent blue.  
After opening the simulation, you can see that the back-up plate is not only fixed but also no longer involved in any collision calculations.  
The dragged material will pass directly through it.  
This also means that in the simulation, the back-up plate is a relatively frozen plate with less calculation.  

After stopping the simulation, return to the state without wearing a mask.  
On the plate, you will see the back-up plate again.  
In addition, at the bottom of the back-up plate, there are options for the back-up plate and the sewing line.  
If you choose the back-up plate and the sewing line, not only will the plate fail, but the sewing line relationship associated with it will also temporarily break, and the sewing line will turn white.  

Take this suit as an example.  
On one side, there is the back-up plate.  
On the other side, the back-up plate and the sewing line.  
You will find that the back-up plate retains the sewing line relationship with the sleeve plate on one side.  
On the other side, the back-up plate and the sewing line are reversed.  
The back-up plate is essentially temporarily non-existent, and the sewing line relationship is also broken.  

Stop the simulation.  
Activate the sewing curve.  
Simulate to stabilize.  

In actual application, when adjusting clothing shape and simulating complex clothing, you can use freeze and counter-activation to fix the plate shape and reduce computation, thereby increasing simulation efficiency.  

For example, now we need to move the belt from the left side of the shirt skirt to the right side.  
If you directly turn on the simulation and drag the belt plate, you will find that the speed of adjusting the belt is slower because the entire garment is involved in the simulation when the belt moves.  

To speed up the simulation and reduce calculation, we can freeze the plate that has direct contact with the belt because the collision calculation between the clothing and belt needs to be maintained—that is, the collision; the other plates not in contact are all counter-activated.  

Then turn on the simulation.  
Adjust the belt position.  
You will find that the simulation speed is much faster.  

After adjusting the belt position,  
in the 3D window,  
on the clothing,  
double-click any position,  
select the whole clothing,  
right-click to select activation.  
Re-model,  
and the belt will naturally be worn.  

Here we see the reset arrangement together.  
Open the reset arrangement file.  
When the clothing appears, how to fix it?  

Take this clothing as an example.  
You can see the bottom of the skirt,  
the collar, and sleeves have problems.  

First, look at the bottom.  
Here, the front and back pieces of the side are made in two different ways.  
The front piece is added directly by the side tool.  
For the wear problem in front of the eye,  
we can directly on the side of the wear,  
right-click to choose arrange initialization,  
which quickly places the side on the inside of the bottom of the front piece,  
then re-model it.  

The back piece of the side is sewn on by the created side plate.  
First, we can also use a similar tool to put the side on the inside of the bottom of the back piece.  
Right-click on the side of the back piece,  
choose to add to the inside,  
and you can add the side to the inside.  

This is suitable for two plates used when there is a seam relationship.  
If the outer layer of the fabric is twisted and the impact is too great, and adding to the inside does not solve it,  
you can select the problematic side first,  
right-click to set the anti-aggression plate and sewing line.  
Note that because it is necessary to completely eliminate the side of the side,  
the option must be anti-aggression plate and sewing line.  

Open the simulation so that the sound is natural and smooth,  
then re-activate the side and add to the inside.  

The problem of overlapping the wrong position of the top and the sleeve can be tried to solve by resetting the 3D arrangement position of the plate.  
We only need to select two plates at the same time.  
Right-click to reset the 3D arrangement position.  
Because these plates have previously used the arrangement point,  
there is memory in the arrangement file,  
and the plate can return to the 3D arrangement state,  
and re-modeling can be restored to normal.  

If the button is stuck in, right-click to reset the button.  
The sleeve and the sleeve plate are also the same operation.  
Select them together,  
right-click to reset the 3D arrangement position.  
You can see that the sleeve plate has been reset to the 3D position,  
and the sleeve plate has no arrangement memory,  
so it is flat.  

In this case,  
we can reopen the virtual model arrangement point,  
select the plate,  
re-select the arrangement point to be arranged,  
or this side-mounted plate,  
you can also directly right-click to add to the side,  
to add the side of the sleeve that has a seam relationship.  

After resetting the position,  
open the simulation,  
this dress is adjusted.  

You can select the basic line of hidden clothing,  
the internal line,  
and the hidden sticky line.  

Switch the clothing rendering type to the dense texture surface  
to check and display the clothing.  

Next, open the library,  
continue to find the selection grid file and open it.  

To make it easier to check,  
you can choose to hide the internal line,  
the hidden basic line,  
and the sticky line.  

The clothing rendering type can also be changed to the dense texture surface.  
You can set it according to your needs.  

When most of the fabric is inside the model's body,  
or when the hitter is in the opposite direction,  
re-modeling may be very time-consuming.  
At this time, we can use the selection grid tool.  

For example,  
see the sleeves of the back shirt are worn onto the arm.  
We will move the part of the plate blocked by the arm to the correct side.  
This can solve this problem.  

Here, we first switch the tool to the selection grid tool.  
In the 3D toolbar,  
the third tool in the first row,  
left-click and hold.  
Here, there are three modes of the selection grid tool brush:  
body, and lock.  
We use the body as an example.  

When using the selection grid tool,  
the plate will automatically display a light green grid.  
Adjust the 3D window angle to the area facing the mask.  
In the 3D window,  
left-click the sleeve part of the frame selection and arm mask.  
Try to select all the mask areas in the frame.  
The selected grid will now become a high-gloss light.  

Then see the 2D panel.  
The corresponding grid will also display light green,  
indicating that it has been selected.  

It can be found that due to some panels being blocked by the arm,  
they cannot be selected.  

Therefore, on the 2D panel,  
in the light green center,  
there will naturally be grids that have not been selected.  
And these grids are also where we need to select and move to the outside of the arm.  

Click on the blank area to cancel the selection.  
According to the memory,  
re-select the frame selection grid on the 2D panel.  
If it is missing,  
you can press Ctrl and Shift to select more.  
If you have selected too many,  
press Ctrl to cancel the selection.  

After the selection is complete,  
in the high-gloss light in the 3D window,  
left-click to remove the positioning ball,  
and turn to the side view.  

Use the positioning ball to align the selected grid to the outside of the arm,  
wrap it around the arm,  
and then turn on the simulation.  

The sleeve mask problem on this side is fixed.  
The other side is the same operation.  
You can practice again.  

The fold and cut of the front pants is the same.  
You can use the same technique to undo the folding this way.  
This is the same process as before.  

Let's first determine which part of the fabric should be on top.  
Then use the selection grid tool to select this part of the grid.  

Note here that we need to move the original fold out of the upper grid.  
Combined with the green high-gloss area,  
we can determine that it should be inside the red line.  
The area on the left needs to be moved out and pulled out.  

Note that you need to move the grid in the stop simulation state,  
otherwise it will move with the surrounding grid.  
If there is no adjustment,  
you can select the grid you need again and move it out.  

In addition, you can select the grid brush and brush tool,  
but the way of selection is different.  
The brush tool can be selected when selecting an irregular grid area,  
and it is custom-made to create a selection area.  
You can also press Ctrl and Shift to select more,  
and press Ctrl to select less.  
The brush can be applied directly on the grid,  
and you can select the grid brush that you want to select.  
Right-click to divide the grid, freeze, print, and so on.  

Finally, you can see the setting layer.  
Open this file.  
Take this layer as an example.  
Now there are two layers here:  
the belt and elastic band of this layer.  

We need to add another belt layer for this layer.  
On the belt layer,  
right-click and select the inner layer of the grid layer.  

Because the new grid layer is only attached to the original layer,  
it will exist with the elastic band of the original layer.  
Direct simulation may not be stable.  

Find the fourth tool in the second row of the 2D toolbar.  
Set the layer.  

First, click on the elastic band layer,  
then click on the inner layer of the grid layer.  

See the arrow point on the 2D layer.  
Layer 1 is the starting point of the arrow.  
The arrow points to layer 2,  
and there is a plus sign on both lines.  

This means that we have set the outside front of plate 1 on plate 2.  
Similarly, set the outside of plate 2 on plate 3.  
That is, a layer of waist fabric on plate 1,  
a layer of elastic band on plate 2,  
a layer of inner waist fabric on plate 3.  
Such a structure.  

After establishing the layer relationship,  
the simulation will be very smooth.  

Here is another detail.  
We are on the left side.  
Change the clothing rendering type to the physical surface  
to distinguish the front and back of the fabric.  

You can see that the inner layer of the curtain is facing outside.  
In other words, what we see is the opposite of the inner layer of the plate.  

If we want the inner layer to be the front of the skin,  
we need to turn the right arrow on the plate to the surface.  

After turning,  
the original layer logic changes.  
Set the plus sign on the layer line.  
It represents a plate on the outside front of another plate.  

Now the inner layer is turned over.  
The front and back are switched.  
The elastic band is now equivalent to the back of it.  

So we are going to change the plus sign of the connection to the minus sign.  
On the plus sign,  
the button can be switched to the minus sign.  

That is, plate 2 is on the front of plate 3.  
It is now on the side of plate 3.  

Finally, about the more detailed explanation of the setting layer,  
you can click the jump link at the bottom of the video  
to jump to the skill video.  

The above are a few tools to improve simulation stability.  
You can practice more.  
If you want to learn more,  
please subscribe to the channel.  

Thank you for watching.  
See you in the next video.

chunks.content: ## Introduction to 3D Clothing Simulation Control in CLO This section introduces fundamental tools and techniques for controlling 3D clothing simulation in CLO, focusing on the use of frozen and back-up plates to manage simulation behavior and improve efficiency. Key terms include **frozen plates**, **back-up plates**, **collision calculation**, and **simulation activation**. - In the Connect tab under the CloudTraining account, unlock the **simulation control** keyword. - Open the frozen and back-up file to work with a shirt skirt model. - Select the belt on the shirt skirt in the 3D window. - Right-click and choose **Frozen**, then press Ctrl-K. The frozen plate appears light blue and its position and shape are fixed during simulation; it does not move when dragged. - Despite being frozen, physical contact and collision with soft clothing beneath still occur. - Right-click on the plate again, unlock the belt, switch to the back-up plate, and press Ctrl-J. The back-up plate turns translucent blue. - When simulated, the back-up plate is fixed and does not participate in collision calculations; materials pass through it. - This means the back-up plate behaves as a frozen plate with reduced computational load. ## Managing Sewing Line Relationships and Simulation Efficiency This section explains how back-up plates interact with sewing lines and how freezing plates can optimize simulation speed by reducing unnecessary calculations. - After stopping simulation, the back-up plate and associated sewing line options appear. - Selecting both back-up plate and sewing line temporarily disables the plate and breaks the sewing line relationship, causing the sewing line to turn white. - Example with a suit: on one side, the back-up plate retains sewing line connections; on the other, selecting both breaks the sewing line and makes the plate temporarily non-existent. - Activating sewing curves and simulating stabilizes the garment after adjustments. - Freezing and counter-activation (disabling) of plates fix shapes and reduce computation, increasing simulation efficiency. ## Practical Example: Adjusting Belt Position on a Shirt Skirt This section details a procedure to efficiently reposition a belt on a garment by selectively freezing and activating plates to speed up simulation. - Directly dragging the belt with simulation on is slow because the entire garment simulates. - To speed this up, freeze plates in direct contact with the belt to maintain collision calculation, and counter-activate other plates not in contact. - Turn on simulation, adjust the belt position; simulation runs faster. - After adjustment, double-click the garment in the 3D window, select the whole clothing, right-click, and choose **activation**. - Re-modeling will naturally wear the adjusted belt. ## Resetting 3D Arrangement and Fixing Clothing Fit Issues This section covers tools and workflows for fixing garment fit problems by resetting arrangement points, managing sewing lines, and adjusting plate layering. - Example issues: bottom of skirt, collar, and sleeves may have fit problems. - For the skirt bottom front piece, use **arrange initialization** to quickly place the side on the inside of the front bottom piece, then re-model.

chunks.content: - Re-modeling will naturally wear the adjusted belt. ## Resetting 3D Arrangement and Fixing Clothing Fit Issues This section covers tools and workflows for fixing garment fit problems by resetting arrangement points, managing sewing lines, and adjusting plate layering. - Example issues: bottom of skirt, collar, and sleeves may have fit problems. - For the skirt bottom front piece, use **arrange initialization** to quickly place the side on the inside of the front bottom piece, then re-model. - Back piece side can be added inside by right-clicking the side and selecting **add to inside**. - For severe fabric twisting where adding inside doesn't help, select the side plate, right-click, and set **anti-aggression plate and sewing line** to eliminate overlap. - Open simulation to smooth movement, then re-activate the side and add it inside. - Overlapping issues between top and sleeve can be solved by selecting both plates and right-clicking **reset 3D arrangement position**, restoring previous arrangement memory. - If buttons get stuck, right-click to reset the button. - Sleeves and sleeve plates can be reset similarly. - For plates without arrangement memory, reopen virtual model arrangement point, select the plate, and re-select the arrangement point. - Plates with seam relationships can be added by right-clicking and choosing **add to side**. - After resetting, open simulation to check garment adjustment. ## Clothing Rendering and Line Visibility Settings This section explains rendering options and line visibility adjustments to facilitate checking garment structure during simulation. - You can toggle visibility of **basic lines**, **internal lines**, and **hidden sticky lines**. - Switch clothing rendering type to **dense texture surface** for detailed fabric display. - Use line visibility options to hide or show specific lines as needed. - These settings help clarify garment structure during fitting and simulation. ## Using the Selection Grid Tool to Fix Fabric Overlaps and Folding This section introduces the **selection grid tool** for correcting fabric overlaps, folds, and misplacements, especially when fabric is obscured by body parts. - When fabric is inside the model body or blocked by opposite direction hits, re-modeling can be slow. - Use the selection grid tool (third tool in the first row of the 3D toolbar) with three modes: **body**, **grid**, and **lock**; body mode is commonly used. - The tool overlays a light green grid on plates. - Adjust the 3D view to face the mask area, then left-click and drag to select sleeve parts behind the arm. - Selected grids become highlighted in high-gloss light green. - In the 2D panel, corresponding grids also highlight green. - Some grids blocked by the arm may remain unselected; select these manually in 2D. - Use Ctrl and Shift keys to add or remove from the selection. - After selection, use the positioning ball to move the selected grids to the outside of the arm and wrap fabric correctly. - Turn on simulation to confirm sleeve mask issues are fixed. - Repeat for the other side as needed.

chunks.content: - In the 2D panel, corresponding grids also highlight green. - Some grids blocked by the arm may remain unselected; select these manually in 2D. - Use Ctrl and Shift keys to add or remove from the selection. - After selection, use the positioning ball to move the selected grids to the outside of the arm and wrap fabric correctly. - Turn on simulation to confirm sleeve mask issues are fixed. - Repeat for the other side as needed. - Similar method applies to undoing folds and cuts on pants. - Select fabric part that should be on top using the selection grid tool and move fold grids out while simulation is stopped. - Brush tool can also be used for irregular grid selections, enabling custom area selection, division, freezing, or printing of grids. ## Managing Layer Relationships for Complex Garments This section describes setting up multiple fabric layers (such as belts and elastic bands) correctly to ensure smooth simulation and proper fabric orientation. - Example: belt and elastic band layers on a garment. - Add a new belt layer by right-clicking and selecting **inner layer of the grid layer**. - The new grid layer is attached to the original, existing alongside the elastic band. - Direct simulation may be unstable without proper layer relationships. - Use the fourth tool in the second row of the 2D toolbar to set layers. - Click on the elastic band layer, then on the inner layer grid layer. - Arrows between layers indicate the relationship: Layer 1 points to Layer 2, with plus signs indicating “outside front” relationships. - Structure example: - Layer 1: waist fabric - Layer 2: elastic band - Layer 3: inner waist fabric - Properly setting layer relationships ensures smooth simulation. ## Adjusting Fabric Orientation and Layer Logic This section explains how to identify and correct fabric front and back orientation by changing rendering types and flipping layers. - Switch clothing rendering type to **physical surface** to distinguish fabric front and back. - For some inner layers, the visible side may be the fabric’s back. - To make the inner layer face outward, flip the plate orientation by turning the arrow on the plate to the surface. - Flipping changes the original layer logic, switching front/back relationships. - The plus sign on layer connections indicates a plate is on the outside front of another plate. - After flipping, change the plus sign to a minus sign by clicking it to update the relationship. - For example, plate 2 becomes on the front side of plate 3 instead of the outside. - This operation ensures inner layers display correctly relative to outer layers and elastic bands. ## Summary of Tools to Improve Simulation Stability This section summarizes key tools and techniques demonstrated to improve 3D clothing simulation stability and efficiency in CLO. - Use **frozen plates** and **back-up plates** to fix garment parts and reduce collision calculations.

For further detailed tutorials on layer settings and advanced simulation techniques, refer to supplementary CLO skill videos.
